🇲🇽📈 <u>ONE SECTOR CARRIED HALF OF MEXICO'S Q2 GROWTH</u>

Wholesale commerce surged 11.3% in Q2 and single-handedly delivered almost half of Mexico's growth — nearly 1 of the 2.1 percentage points the economy advanced, per El Financiero's Enrique Quintana citing INEGI. Strip it out and growth falls to about 1.2%. Five sectors — wholesale, construction, agriculture, mining and government — account for 84% of the annual gain, a rebound that's real but unusually concentrated.

🇲🇽🏥 <u>MEXICO CITY ADDS 800 FREE CLINICS TO ITS UNIVERSAL HEALTH SYSTEM</u>

Mexico City is folding 800 neighborhood clinics into a universal public health system — free consultations, labs, medicines, mental-health care and chronic-disease screening for everyone, regardless of job or income. It's one slice of a federal rollout of 12,750 clinics across 24 states. "We have a historic opportunity to produce health in the territories," said Mayor Clara Brugada.

🇲🇽🌹 <u>MORENA LINES UP ITS 2027 SLATE — AND WOMEN ARE LEADING IT</u>

Morena named Rosi Bayardo, ex-mayor of Manzanillo, as its Colima coordinator and likely 2027 gubernatorial candidate — one of several women, alongside Nora Ruvalcaba in Aguascalientes, the party is advancing for the next cycle. Bayardo, a psychologist who's organized the state since 2017, contrasted the 4T's Colima with the "financial crisis" the PRI-PAN administration left behind.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>US AND CANADA SOUND ALARMS OVER MEXICALI — MEXICO SAYS SHOW THE EVIDENCE</u>

The US Consulate in Tijuana and Canada both issued security alerts over a vague "threat" in Mexicali, telling citizens to avoid public buildings. Mexico's Security Cabinet checked and pushed back: "there are no elements that confirm a specific or imminent risk." Patrols were reinforced anyway, but the pattern is familiar — foreign alarm bells over Mexican cities, no evidence attached.

🇲🇽⚖️ <u>AFTER 200 YEARS, MEXICO'S INDIGENOUS PEOPLES GET A VOICE IN THE COURTS</u>

For the first time, Mexico's Supreme Court ruled that Indigenous communities can intervene in constitutional controversies — proceedings once reserved for state powers. The 5-4 vote let the Mazahua people of Crescencio Morales be heard in their own case. "Today we're seeing whether we correct 200 years of exclusion, racism and the judicial exclusion of Indigenous peoples," said Chief Justice Hugo Aguilar Ortiz, the reformed court's first Mixtec president.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>CIA HAS PERSONNEL IN MEXICO — AND IT ANSWERS TO MEXICAN LAW</u>

Sheinbaum confirmed from the National Palace that the CIA keeps personnel inside Mexico — and that they operate strictly under Mexican terms: "they are complying with what the National Security Law establishes." It comes four months after two CIA agents died running an unauthorized narco-lab operation alongside Chihuahua's PAN state government, a case the FGR is still investigating for violating the Constitution.
